name: Basin-edge geophysics: buried range-front faults
signature: Co-location of three independent expressions of one buried structure: (a) a step in depth-to-basement, (b) a resistivity contrast between bedrock and basin fill, (c) a gravity gradient. Implemented as normalised-convolution gradient magnitude, Hessian crestness and Hessian anisotropy of each field at 150 m and 400 m, plus a 9x9 coherence of the basement-step direction.
why_new_faults: A Great Basin range front buried under basin fill has almost no topographic expression, so a scarp-based catalogue systematically misses it, while its basin geometry is obvious in MT/airborne-EM depth-to-basement and in gravity. Range-front faults are also the geothermal targets the prize cares about. Individually depth_to_base_surf (AUC 0.512) and cond_surf (0.483) are near-uninformative; the information is in their co-location with a gravity gradient, which no shipped layer expresses.
differs_from: The existing stack uses these three fields only as raw amplitudes. Nothing in it combines them into a coincidence or step-coherence measure, and no shipped layer targets the bedrock/basin-fill contact.
external_data_needed: none - all three layers ship with the competition
outcome: REJECTED - slightly worse than baseline on 6 blocked folds; within noise but not positive

name: Scarp-facing coherence: persistent anisotropy of the 1 m DEM gradient
signature: |mean unit gradient| / mean |gradient| of the field over 9x9 and 21x21 windows. A single through-going scarp drives this toward 1 regardless of its height; dissected terrain, dune fields and drainage texture drive it toward 0.
why_new_faults: The catalogue is amplitude-biased: it contains the tall, obvious scarps. The faults it is missing are disproportionately the low-relief but long and straight ones. Coherence is deliberately amplitude-blind, so a 1 m scarp that runs for 5 km outranks a 5 m scarp in broken ground - reversing the ranking the catalogue itself was built on.
differs_from: The existing stack measures scarp amplitude (lid_relief, ex_max, step_max) and single-scale curvature (lappos_max, lapneg_max). Nothing measures persistence of facing direction across a window, which is a different physical property.
external_data_needed: none - uses the owner-mirrored 1 m DEM scarp stack already present
outcome: ADOPTED - best arm: +0.0058 in-block AUC and +0.0023 proxy DTI over baseline, consistent in sign

name: Trace-tip continuation corridors
signature: Extract the endpoints of every mapped trace (catalogue pixels with at most one 8-neighbour catalogue pixel) and feed log-distance-to-nearest-tip into the detector, so the model can learn how fault likelihood decays away from a mapped tip.
why_new_faults: The organizer confirmed in writing that 'new fault' means any fault pixel not already captured and explicitly includes newly mapped geometry of an existing fault system - continuations, splays, parallel strands. The corridor just beyond a mapped tip is therefore the single highest-prior location for an unmapped fault pixel.
differs_from: Distance-to-catalogue is already in the stack but is measured to the nearest fault pixel anywhere along a trace, which is dominated by the trace interior and is also a perfect training leak (IR-51-LEAK-01). Distance-to-tip is a different quantity and is used only at emission time.
cost: low (built; recomputed per fold from the fold's known catalogue only)
outcome: REJECTED - clearly harmful. Distance-to-trace-tip is a partial catalogue leak: tips come from the known catalogue, so near-tip pixels in the training set are themselves catalogue pixels, and the feature does not transfer into an unmapped block

name: Geodetic strain-budget deficit over broad tiles (the owner's hypothesis)
layers: comp_geod_2ndinv (geodetic second invariant of the strain rate tensor)
gdr_qfaults_traces.csv numeric slip_rate (USGS alias mm/year; exact component semantics unresolved) + slip_sense, with trace length from the catalogue raster
signature: Kreemer et al. (2000) Eq. 3 moment-tensor sum of trace length and assumed slip-rate component into a per-tile horizontal tensor; subtract quantile-ranked fault-accommodated II from quantile-ranked geodetic II. Source slip-rate component and sense fallbacks are unresolved assumptions, tested as vertical versus total fault-plane rate and unknown-as-normal versus known-sense-only.
why_new_faults: Tiles where geodesy demands more deformation than the mapped faults can supply are the tiles where the catalogue is likeliest to be incomplete.
differs_from: Stage 1, entirely new to this repository. Retained strictly as a coarse tile prior, never as a point placer, because the owner's own history shows habitat-style statements scored 0.0041, 0.1223 and 0.1352.
expected_dti: small as a standalone emitter - used as a gate, and measured as such
cost: medium (built: Kostrov summation, tile aggregation, quantile deficit, H and dip sensitivity)
external_data_needed: none for current experiment; local GDR-derived table mirrors QFaults, but field component semantics are not authenticated from the archive definitions.
outcome: RETAINED AS BROAD-TILE PRIOR ONLY; not a locator. Five trace-level splits across four rate/sense assumptions: mean Spearman deficit +0.027 to +0.032 versus +0.099 for geodetic-only; q50 lift 1.097–1.104 versus 1.239. Random-dot DTI is one seeded draw per field/split and unpaired across masks. The six-fold pre-revision soft w=0.10 sweep gives exact mean ΔDTI +0.000367 (4/6 folds); small/inconclusive, not a win. Hard q20/top-80% gate loses about 0.0025. Formula/source/field semantics are audited in evidence/stage1_formula_audit.json and evidence/submission_manifest_reconciliation.json.

name: Cross-catalogue discrepancy (SGMC minus INGENIOUS)
layers: derived_sgmc_faults_100m_u8 (USGS SGMC faults rasterised to the competition grid)
signature: Boolean XOR: pixels where the USGS SGMC compilation shows a fault and the INGENIOUS catalogue does not.
why_new_faults: Two national compilations were built independently by different workers at different times. Where they disagree, one of them has a fault the other lacks, and the scoring catalogue is the INGENIOUS one.
differs_from: sgmc_fault is in the base stack as a raw layer; the discrepancy product is not.
expected_dti: low - and there is direct prior evidence against it
prior_evidence_against: GEMSDOE29 shipped 'sgmc-off-catalogue-44k' and it scored 0.0512, and GEMSDOE32 measured that 59,065 SGMC-derived px all but one lie within 300 m of the given catalogue, i.e. the discrepancy product is nearly empty once the catalogue is accounted for
outcome: NOT RUN AS A STANDALONE ARM - prior evidence against it is already strong (GEMSDOE29 shipped sgmc-off-catalogue-44k and scored 0.0512; GEMSDOE32 measured that 59,065 SGMC-derived px all but one lie within 300 m of the given catalogue). The sgmc_fault layer is retained inside the baseline feature stack.

name: 1 m 3DEP DEM re-derivation of the scarp stack (NOT VIABLE IN THIS SANDBOX)
signature: Re-derive scarp height, asymmetry and facing directly from 1 m lidar/3DEP tiles instead of using the owner's 100 m aggregate.
why_new_faults: The 100 m aggregate throws away the sub-pixel scarp geometry that a fault mapper actually reads.
differs_from: Would replace rather than extend the existing scarp stack.
external_data_needed: USGS 3DEP / The National Map 1 m DEM tiles. Official and free: https://www.usgs.gov/3d-elevation-program and https://apps.nationalmap.gov/downloader/ . This candidate cannot be validated here and is NOT proposed as viable without a machine with unrestricted egress.
outcome: BLOCKED - external data not obtainable from this sandbox (measured)
